tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

  unsaved edits.
- **Filament, when the target is another preset.** The preset must be in one
  of the project's slots; otherwise the call fails with `not_in_project`. It
  can be changed only by saving, so a call without `persistAs` fails with
  `not_selected`. Apply opens the preset in the filament tab the way the
  sidebar's edit button does: `Tab::select_preset`, then `set_filament_idx`
  for its slot. Apply then loads the change and saves it through the tab. If
  the filament that is open in the tab has unsaved edits, that switch would
  either discard them or show a prompt. So preview refuses with
  `unsaved_edits`.
- **Printer, when the target is another preset.** This is a saved printer
  that the project does not use. It can only be saved in place. The write
  goes through `Printers::write_unselected_printer`, which is the write
  `change_named_printer_nozzle` already makes: it stores the difference from
  the parent preset and queues the change for the cloud. Saving a copy of it
  would quietly create a second printer that the project does not know
  about. So a different `persistAs` fails with `not_selected`.
- A printer's blocked keys are the ones that decide which filament and
  process fit, or how many extruders there are (bed shape, nozzle size and
  type, extruder count, printer model), its network address and sign-in,
  and its identity as a preset. Those are 43 of its 160 settings. Custom
  g-code stays writable for a printer and a filament, as it was.
- Some settings hold one value per extruder or per nozzle kind. Such a
  setting keeps its length. A patch with a different number of values fails
  with `invalid_setting_value`, because a shorter list would drop the rest.

`persistAs` is not valid for `object`. For the preset scopes it works like
OrcaSlicer's Save with the name typed in:

- The preset's own name overwrites the preset. If OrcaSlicer ships that
  preset, the call fails with `read_only_preset`, and the suggestion is
  `"<name> - Copy"`, the name SavePresetDialog offers.
- Another name that no preset has saves a copy, and the copy takes the
  original's place. For a filament, that happens in every project slot that
  used the original (`Sidebar::update_presets_from_to`).
- A name that another preset has fails with `name_taken`.
- A name that SavePresetDialog would refuse fails with
  `invalid_preset_name`.

Saving the preset that is being edited also saves its other unsaved edits, as
Save does. Preview warns about this with `saves_unsaved_edits` and lists
those edits. The card's title says where the change is saved ("; save it", or
"; save as \"<name>\""). Without `persistAs`, the tool changes only the
edited preset and leaves it dirty.

- a max volumetric speed below 0.5

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before

# No save prompts in agent tools: report

Commit a165018fc8 on branch `claude/no-save-prompts` (based on origin/jusprin-newui 20de313d92). Not pushed.

## Problem

On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin should never ask a person to save or discard: autosave keeps the work, and version history is the way back. Several paths built earlier still asked or refused:

- `project_open` refused when the project or a preset had unsaved changes, unless the agent passed `unsavedWork: "discard"` after asking the user. `printer_setup` did the same with `unsavedEdits` when a preset switch would drop edits.
- `settings_preview_patch` refused with `unsaved_edits` when saving a filament other than the one open in the filament tab, while the open one had edits.
- A filament save whose first-layer temperature was more than 30 °C from the other layers' (15 °C for a bed) was refused, because OrcaSlicer asks "Continue anyway?" before such a save.
- `Plater::load_project` called `file_open_can_replace_project`, which stopped any file open over unsaved changes with "Opening stopped…". This check ran before the autosave hook, and the agent prompt told the model to ask the user whether to save or discard.

## What happens now

- `project_open` always starts with Orca's `new_project`, which runs the autosave hook. The hook saves the open project, edited presets included. If that save fails, the tool returns "The open project could not be saved, so it stays open" and nothing else happens. After the save, edited presets are dropped and the file loads.
- `printer_setup` drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in `discarded`. The before-state is pinned, as it is for every agent change.
- Saving another filament drops the open filament's unsaved edits. Preview lists them in a `discards_unsaved_edits` warning. The `saves_unsaved_edits` warning stays.
- The temperature check is now an `orca_question` warning in OrcaSlicer's words, with the first-layer values Orca accepts as `min` and `max`. Apply answers Continue on Orca's dialog. The max-volumetric-speed refusal is unchanged.
- The "Opening stopped" check, its message and its prompt row are deleted. The tool descriptions and the tool guide now describe what happens, with no mention of asking.

**Finding on the old check:** it fired even with autosave running. Autosave writes with `SaveStrategy::Backup`, and that never resets the saved timestamp that `Plater::up_to_date(false, false)` reads. In the shell harness, after `autosave()->save_now()` succeeded on a changed project, `up_to_date` still returned false. So every open over a changed project was stopped, in the GUI too.

## Tests and results

All pass on a Release build:

- agent_bridge_tests: 276 cases
- workspace_contract_tests: 41 cases
- AgentUI vitest: 410 tests
- workspace adapter harness: 5,934 checks
- shell harness: 547 checks, 0 failures

New real-adapter cases:

- The forwarded save question matches the text of Orca's own dialog, which also shows a "Don't warn again" checkbox label after the question.
- The save goes ahead with no dialog.
- A save to another filament drops the open filament's edits, with no dialog.

The shell harness checks that a person's own open over a changed project, and the same open through the tool, both run without a dialog.

## Remaining issues

- `project_open` now calls `new_project` even when the project is clean. If a 3MF then fails to load, the project is left empty. This was already the case for a changed project, and `load_project` clears the old model in the same way.
- Two printer flows still refuse in save-or-discard words: printer connect and change in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp` (around lines 363 and 406), and a nozzle change when the printer preset has unsaved edits. They were not part of this task.

**Line count:** 180 lines added, 183 removed (net −3). Without tests and docs: 86 added, 129 removed. `AgentHost.cpp` is untouched.

The agent tools no longer ask the user to save or discard. Opening a project, switching presets and saving filament settings all go ahead now, and autosave and version history keep what would otherwise be lost. The commit is a165018fc8 on branch `claude/no-save-prompts`, based on origin/jusprin-newui 20de313d92, and is not pushed. It adds 180 lines and removes 183 (net −3). Leaving out tests and docs, it adds 86 and removes 129.

**What changed:**
- **`project_open`**: the `unsavedWork` parameter and its refusal are gone. The tool now starts with OrcaSlicer's `new_project`, which runs the autosave hook (`m_before_project_release`). The hook does run on this path. It saves the open project, including edited presets. If that save fails, the tool returns "The open project could not be saved, so it stays open" and nothing else happens. After the save, edited presets are dropped and the file loads.
- **`printer_setup`**: the `unsavedEdits` parameter and its refusal are gone. It drops unsaved preset edits and lists them in the result's `discarded` field, as before.
- **Settings preview, saving a filament other than the one open in its tab**: this used to be refused with `unsaved_edits`. It now goes ahead. The open filament's edits are dropped, and a `discards_unsaved_edits` warning lists them. The `saves_unsaved_edits` warning is kept.
- **Save-time temperature check**: it is now an `orca_question` warning in OrcaSlicer's words. Its `min` and `max` are the first-layer temperatures OrcaSlicer accepts. When the save runs, the tool answers OrcaSlicer's "Continue anyway?" dialog with Continue. The volumetric-speed refusal is unchanged.
- **"Opening stopped" check**: `file_open_can_replace_project`, its message and the matching row in `fileReportInstructions.ts` are deleted. No test covered that row.
- **Descriptions and guide**: the two tool descriptions in `ToolRegistry.cpp` and `mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` now describe what happens, with no mention of asking.
- `AgentHost.cpp` is untouched, so it should merge cleanly with the other two tasks.

**The "Opening stopped" check still fired with autosave running.** Autosave saves through `export_3mf` with `SaveStrategy::Backup`, which never resets the timestamp that `Plater::up_to_date(false, false)` reads. In the shell harness, I made a project dirty and ran `autosave()->save_now()`. The save succeeded, and `up_to_date` still returned false. So before this change, every open over a changed project was stopped, including a person's own File > Open in the GUI.

**Tests:** everything passes on a Release build in this worktree. No live model was called.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| agent_bridge_tests | 276 test cases pass |
| workspace_contract_tests | 41 test cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest | 410 tests pass |
| Workspace adapter harness (real adapter) | 5,934 checks pass, exit 0 |
| Shell harness | 547 checks, 0 failures, exit 0 |

I added two cases to the workspace adapter harness:
- **Save-time question**: the forwarded text matches OrcaSlicer's own dialog word for word. The comparison allows for the "Don't warn again" checkbox label the dialog shows after the question. The save then completes with no dialog.
- **Saving another filament**: the open filament's edits are dropped, and nothing asks.

The shell harness now checks that a person's own open over a changed project, and the same open through `project_open`, both run with no dialog.

**Left as they were:**
- `project_open` now calls `new_project` even on a clean project. If a 3MF then fails to load, the project is left empty. That already happened when the project was dirty, and `load_project` clears the old model the same way.
- Two printer flows still refuse in save-or-discard words: printer connect and change in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp` (around lines 363 and 406), and a nozzle change when the printer preset has unsaved edits. They weren't in this task's list.

The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. 3	Commit c1e4ee88ce on branch `claude/no-save-prompts`, rebased onto the force-pushed origin/jusprin-newui 7b2441dfd4 ("Rename ToolExecutionCoordinator::propose to submit"). Not pushed.
4	
5	## Problem
6	
7	On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin should never ask a person to save or discard: autosave keeps the work, and version history is the way back. Several paths built earlier still asked or refused:
8	
9	- `project_open` refused when the project or a preset had unsaved changes, unless the agent passed `unsavedWork: "discard"` after asking the user. `printer_setup` did the same with `unsavedEdits` when a preset switch would drop edits.
10	- `settings_preview_patch` refused with `unsaved_edits` when saving a filament other than the one open in the filament tab, while the open one had edits.
11	- A filament save whose first-layer temperature was more than 30 °C from the other layers' (15 °C for a bed) was refused, because OrcaSlicer asks "Continue anyway?" before such a save.
...
20	- The "Opening stopped" check, its message and its prompt row are deleted. The tool descriptions and the tool guide now describe what happens, with no mention of asking.
21	
22	**Finding on the old check:** it fired even with autosave running. Autosave writes with `SaveStrategy::Backup`, and that never resets the saved timestamp that `Plater::up_to_date(false, false)` reads. In the shell harness, after `autosave()->save_now()` succeeded on a changed project, `up_to_date` still returned false. So every open over a changed project was stopped, in the GUI too.

39

Yes, the task is complete, and it is rebased onto the force-pushed jusprin-newui.

**Rebase:** My change now sits on top of the new jusprin-newui head, 7b2441dfd4, as commit c1e4ee88ce on `claude/no-save-prompts`. The only conflict was in the coordinator unit tests, where the other task renamed `propose` to `submit`. I kept the new name and my edits. The size didn't change: 180 lines added, 183 removed, so 3 fewer than before. `AgentHost.cpp` is still untouched.

**Tests:** I rebuilt and reran everything on the rebased code, and all of it passes:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent bridge tests | 273 cases pass (the new base removed 3) |
| Workspace contract tests | 41 cases pass |
| AgentUI vitest | 410 tests pass |
| Workspace adapter harness | 5,934 checks pass |
| Shell harness | 550 checks, 0 failures |

I didn't call any live model. I updated the untracked report, [no-save-prompts-report.md](no-save-prompts-report.md), with the new commit, base and counts.

**What the change does:**
- **Opening a project:** the agent no longer refuses or asks when the project has unsaved changes. Autosave saves the project first, then the new file opens. If that save fails, the tool reports an error and the old project stays open.
- **Switching printer presets, or saving a different filament:** unsaved preset edits are dropped without asking, and the result says what was dropped.
- **Temperature question on save:** OrcaSlicer's "Continue anyway?" question about first-layer temperatures is now a warning in OrcaSlicer's own words. The agent decides what to do with it, the same way it handles the edit-time questions.
- **"Opening stopped" check:** removed. It blocked every open over a changed project, even with autosave running, because autosave never resets the "unsaved" flag that check reads.

**Questions for you:**
1. Should I push the branch `claude/no-save-prompts`? I haven't, because you said not to.
2. Two printer flows still refuse with "save or discard" wording: connecting or changing a named printer when its preset has unsaved edits, and changing the nozzle size in that case. They weren't on your list, so I left them alone. Do you want them changed the same way, in a separate task?
3. One small behaviour change to confirm. `project_open` now always starts a new project before loading, even when nothing is unsaved. If a project file then fails to load, you're left with an empty project rather than the previous one. Before, that only happened when there were unsaved changes, and OrcaSlicer's own load already clears the old model before loading. The previous project is in version history either way. Is that acceptable?

content.content:
The conclusion is that a definition adds cost to the *first* request of each conversation, not to every turn. That is why going over the budget only makes us look at the measurements and does not block a tool. Two things would change this conclusion: a catalog so large that the first request of every conversation is expensive by itself, or transcripts that show the model choosing the wrong tool. Watch for both. Neither has appeared yet.

**The printer panel follows the same rule with its own set of tools.** The printer panel on Home runs its own conversation, `PrinterConversation`. That conversation is offered the five printer tools and the four settings tools. The list is the same in every mode (Add, Change, or Connect), so it stays byte-identical through a conversation and between conversations of the same mode.

What a call may do depends on the conversation. `PrinterConversation::preflight_tool` refuses every call that is not allowed, before any card is shown, with an error that says where to go instead. The rules are:

- Finding and adding a printer (`printer_identify`, `printer_add`) is allowed only in an Add conversation. A Change or Connect conversation is about a printer the person already has. An add there would save another printer and move the conversation onto it.
- `printer_change` is allowed only on the printer the conversation is about, once there is one.
- The connection tools are allowed only once there is a saved printer.
- The settings tools are allowed only with `scope: "printer"`, on the printer the conversation is about.

A Change conversation may be about a stock profile (one that ships with OrcaSlicer) that the project has selected. That happens when the person chooses Printer settings… in the header on a project that uses a stock profile. In that case, changes to the nozzle and to the connection are refused with `stock_profile`. Changes to settings are saved as a copy of the profile, and the conversation follows that copy from then on (`PrinterConversation::tool_settled`). A Change conversation is never turned into an Add conversation. The code that opens a Change conversation checks that the printer is there, and shows OrcaSlicer's error dialog when it is not.

The header's filament chat uses the same panel (`PrinterPanel::open_filament`). It is offered the four settings tools and nothing else, and it gets no project state. It has its own instructions. The page writes them in `AgentUI/src/filamentInstructions.ts` and sends them with `filament_instructions`. The page writes them from the facts the app sends as the session part of the panel's state (`PrinterPanel::filament_session_json`): the preset's name, its slot and material, and, for a stock filament, the copy that a change is saved as. The preflight check for this chat allows the settings tools only with `scope: "filament"` on that preset. It refuses an apply that has no `persistAs`, with `not_saved`, because the chat is gone when it closes. When a copy is saved in the preset's place, the chat is about that copy from then on, and the page writes the instructions again for the copy. Until 2026-09-29 the filament chat ran on the project assistant's instructions and tools. With those, the model read "make the nozzle 5 degrees hotter" as a request to print. In another run it set 205 °C when the value was 220 °C, without reading the value first.

A nozzle change from the panel would really have lost the dropped edits. The panel now saves a version first, the same way the main agent pane does before any change to the project. A test changes the nozzle through the panel, restores the version saved before it, and finds the dropped edit. I removed the new step and confirmed that the test fails without it.
- **Connect:** it no longer refuses. It only ever wrote the three connection settings, so the project's other unsaved edits stay, and nothing is dropped.
- **Rename:** it no longer opens Orca's save-or-discard prompt. I kept the edits instead of dropping them. Renaming saves the profile under its new name, and the unsaved edits are put back, still unsaved, on the same printer. Renaming a printer the project isn't using briefly selects it. If that switch dropped the project printer's edits, renaming some other printer would lose them, which would be surprising. If you'd rather have rename drop the edits, it's a small change.

The agent's `project_open` doesn't check either.

"Continue current project" would then quietly keep the old geometry. If the file's contents differ, the prompt should say so and make "Create new project" the default. whether to create another project or open the existing one directly. If several
projects match, it continues the current one when it came from that file;

path still offers the choice.

current-document format without rewriting historical versions.

opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.

---
name: capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff
description: "How to capture the fork's wx popup menus on macOS for a pixel comparison against Windows captures, and why Windows text renders ~9% larger than the tokens intend."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 08293464-543a-44de-9266-25cac34b4e36
  modified: 2026-09-09T17:42:05.370Z
---

To compare Windows screenshots against macOS, run the same
`shell_integration_harness` fixture on both and capture each popup by window id.

**Why:** `screencapture` and any ScreenCaptureKit path fail from the Bash tool
("could not create image from display") — the Screen Recording grant belongs to a
process I cannot reach. The computer-use `app_screenshot` tool is the only route,
and it accepts a **raw CGWindowID**, not just ids from `app_list_windows`. Popups
never appear in `app_list_windows`, so enumerate them yourself.

**How to apply:**
- Build a tiny Swift lister (`CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(.optionOnScreenOnly)`
  filtered by pid). The fork's `HeaderMenu` popups show up at `layer=101`; the main
  window is `layer=0`. Feed that id to `app_screenshot` for native-resolution pixels.
- Drive clicks with a Swift `CGEvent` helper at **global** coords
  (window origin + local). The app need not be frontmost.
- Only the **chip halves** respond to synthetic clicks. The header's overflow "…",
  the split-button chevron, and the Home back button do not — that is a limitation
  of the automation, **not** an application bug. Use the harness's own
  `--header-visual` / `--review-visual` modes for those screens instead.
- While a popup is open, the next click anywhere only dismisses it. Budget two
  clicks. Escape does not close them.
- Put the window on the **Acer H226HQL** (1920x1080, non-Retina): the harness's
  1200x800 window is then 1:1 with a Windows capture at 100% scaling, so popup
  sizes compare directly. On the built-in Retina display they would not.

**Windows text is ~9% LARGER than macOS, not smaller.** `Label::sysFont`
(`src/slic3r/GUI/Widgets/Label.cpp:19`) multiplies the point size by 4/5 off Apple
to offset Windows' 96 DPI against macOS' 72 — but 96/72 x 4/5 = 1.067, so it
under-corrects. Measured on the chip: glyph height 12 px Windows vs 11 px macOS.
Consequence: fixed-width popups ellipsize *more* on Windows. Do not assume the 4/5
factor makes Windows text smaller. Mono text goes the other way (Courier New is
narrower than Menlo), so the chip itself comes out 346 px on Windows vs 353 on Mac.

See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]],
[[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

name: screenshots-to-files-via-page-fixture
description: "computer_batch save_to_disk produced no files (2026-09-23); to get screenshot files for a report, replay the observed host state into the built Agent/Home page under Playwright, which saves PNGs; plus the window-overlap trap when another session runs the harness."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 49ad3806-419d-49f2-8833-1578cd5bf2b3
  modified: 2026-09-23T21:16:58.377Z
---

On 2026-09-23 a full live walkthrough of the printer panel was driven with display-scope `computer_batch` (`zoom` + `save_to_disk: true`). Every call returned the image, but no path was reported and a disk-wide search found no file. Do not count on `save_to_disk` for deliverables.

**What worked for files:** the [[fake-host-page-fixture]] recipe under the Playwright MCP. Copy `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` (and `home/index.html`), inject `window.wx` + a `window.SCENES` table of full `state` payloads, serve with `python3 -m http.server`, open `agent.html?panel=printer`, switch scenes with `browser_evaluate` and save with `browser_take_screenshot` (`scale: device`, `filename` under the repo's `.playwright-mcp/`, the only allowed root; move the PNGs out and `rm -rf .playwright-mcp` afterwards so `git status` stays clean). Real printer pictures come from `resources/profiles/<Vendor>/<Model>_cover.png` as data URLs. The credential card renders from a `toolActivities` entry with `tool: 'printer_connect'`, `correlationId` = an assistant message id, state `pending` (card) or `succeeded` ("Sent"). Chips come from a trailing `Choices: a | b` line. 13 scenes took about 10 minutes and matched the live rendering.

**Window overlap trap:** when another session runs `JusPrinShellHarness --printer-live` in a loop, each run opens a 1200x800 window at the same origin (360,125) on the primary display and takes the front, so display-scope zooms and clicks land on *its* window. Move your own instance by pid with a 20-line Swift AX helper (`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` → `kAXPositionAttribute`) onto the built-in display (bounds start at y=1080 here), then `switch_display "Built-in Retina Display"`. The first display click only focuses the window; click again. `--manual-live-agent` does not enable the fake Bambu printer, so the Bambu connect path is out of reach in manual mode.

**Why:** the walkthrough's evidence would otherwise have been lost, and a click into the other session's scripted run could have corrupted its result.

**How to apply:** for any "take screenshots" request on the web pages, plan on the fixture route for files from the start and use the live app only to observe. See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[printer-live-harness-lessons]].

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_ax_find
entries.description:
Search the accessibility elements captured by the last app_screenshot of one window. Filter by role (e.g. "AXTextArea", "AXButton") and/or title substring. Returns matching elements with their [N] index — pass that as element_index to app_click/app_type. Use this when the inline summary in app_screenshot doesn't show the element you need (it only lists the first few actionable ones).

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu; hover states and context menus still need the display-scope screenshot/left_click tools (which do take over the screen).

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

role.description: Exact AX role to match (e.g. "AXButton", "AXTextArea", "AXLink", "AXComboBox"). Omit to match any role.

title_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring to match against the element's title. Omit to match any title.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_batch
entries.description:
Execute a sequence of app_* actions against ONE window in a single tool call. Each individual app_* call is a model→API round trip; batching a predictable sequence (e.g. click a field, type into it, press return) eliminates all but one. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error or 'unsupported' result. An 'ineffective' result (write accepted, app didn't visibly respond yet) does NOT stop the batch — include a screenshot action after to verify. Include {"action":"screenshot"} anywhere in the list to capture the window at that point — coordinates and element_index in actions AFTER a screenshot refer to that screenshot. Put one last to see the post-batch state in the same call.

element_index.description: Index into the AX summary returned by the last app_screenshot (the [N] prefix on each line). Targets that element's center directly instead of by coordinate. Refused if something from another page inside the window (an embedded page, or the page around one) is at that position now, or if the action would go to something else of the same page than that element. target.description:
Dispatch against the application's currently-focused UI element (AXFocusedUIElement) instead of hit-testing at a coordinate. Use for canvas-heavy apps (Pages, Keynote) where the document body has no positional accessibility elements but the app's own text cursor is somewhere editable. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and element_index.

path.description: For drag only: [[x, y], ...] points to drag through, first = press, last = release; replaces coordinate + to_coordinate.

entries.description: Bring one of this app's windows from another desktop Space onto the CURRENT Space, out of the Dock when it is minimized, or back on screen when its app is hidden (all windows of that app then come back), so you can act on it in the background. entries.description:

Use for text selection, moving items in a list, or drawing. A drag is delivered as raw input, which in some apps makes the app active for a moment (its windows are not raised) before the previously active app is restored. All points are in the same window-local coordinate space as `app_click`.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_key
entries.description:
Press a key or key combination in one window of a granted application without bringing it to the front. return, escape, backspace and cmd+a act on the element at (x, y) through accessibility when it supports them. Otherwise — and always for tab, shift+tab, the arrow keys up/down/left/right (alone or with shift, cmd or option), home, end, pageup and pagedown — the key goes as a keystroke to whatever has keyboard focus in that window, so app_click the field or list first and check the effect with app_screenshot. Use app_menu for ⌘-shortcuts. A native app in the background ignores a cmd+a keystroke, so it is refused there. To overwrite all the text of ONE text box or shape on a Keynote-style canvas, double-click into it, press cmd+up, then shift+cmd+down, then app_type. Use those two keys only while such a box is being edited: in a document body (Pages, TextEdit) they select the WHOLE document, and in a list or on a selected table cell they do other things. Press escape once; another with nothing left to cancel only plays the Mac's alert sound.

Refused if something from another page inside the window (an embedded page, or the page around one) is at that position now, or if the action would go to something else of the same page than that element. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and target.

target.description:
Dispatch against the application's currently-focused UI element (AXFocusedUIElement) instead of hit-testing at a coordinate. Use for canvas-heavy apps (Pages, Keynote) where the document body has no positional accessibility elements but the app's own text cursor is somewhere editable. Mutually exclusive with coordinate and element_index.

If you omit ALL of coordinate, element_index, and target, the action defaults to the same point as your most recent app_* action on this window — so [click coord, type text, key combo] chains naturally without repeating the coordinate.

overwrite_existing.description: Only relevant when positional insert (set AXSelectedText) doesn't work for this app and the field already has content — in that case the only background fallback is replacing the WHOLE field. By default that is REFUSED (unsupported: would_replace_content) so you don't clobber a draft or document. Set true to proceed; the previous content (≤500 chars) is returned in the result so you can restore it if the replace was wrong.

mode.description: insert (default) writes at the caret/selection. replace selects all then writes, clearing the field in one call — use when you need to overwrite the whole field rather than append. Not for a text box on a Keynote-style canvas: there nothing gets selected first, so old text stays behind; select the box's text first as app_key describes, then insert.

disable_substitutions.description: Disable the app's Text Replacement / autocorrect around this type (so e.g. "backpropagation" is not mangled), then restore the user's prior setting afterward.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every call. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__app_zoom
entries.description:
Get a closer look at part of a window you have already captured with app_screenshot: returns just that region, at the display's full pixel density so small text and fine detail are legible. Reading aid only — it does not replace your app_screenshot: coordinates for app_click and every other app_* tool keep referring to the app_screenshot, never to the zoomed image, and the zoomed image carries no element summary.

This tool acts on one application in the BACKGROUND while the user keeps working in other apps. The target window does not come to the front. For the menu bar use app_menu; hover states and context menus still need the display-scope screenshot/left_click tools (which do take over the screen).

app.description: Bundle identifier of the target application (e.g. "com.apple.TextEdit"). Must be in the granted-applications list — call request_access first if it isn't.

window_id.description: CGWindowID from app_list_windows or from a previous app_screenshot result. If omitted, defaults to the window you most recently app_screenshot-ed for this app (or the app's main window if you haven't screenshotted yet). Pass a different id to switch windows — there is no separate switch-window tool; targeting is per-call via this parameter.

region.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1]: left, top, right, bottom edges of the region, in pixels of the most recent app_screenshot's full-resolution coordinate frame (same space as `coordinate`).

scale.description: Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

entries.name: mcp__computer-use__computer_batch
entries.description: Execute a sequence of actions in ONE tool call. Each individual tool call requires a model→API round trip (seconds); batching a predictable sequence eliminates all but one. Use this whenever you can predict the outcome of several actions ahead — e.g. click a field, type into it, press Return. Actions execute sequentially and stop on the first error. The frontmost application must be in the session allowlist at the time of this call, or this tool returns an error and does nothing. The frontmost check runs before EACH action inside the batch — if an action opens a non-allowed app, the next action's gate fires and the batch stops there. Screenshot and zoom actions are allowed and their images are returned interleaved with the per-action outputs. Coordinates you write in THIS batch — clicks AND zoom regions — always refer to the full-screen screenshot taken BEFORE this call, never to a zoom and never to a mid-batch screenshot. After the batch returns, the most recent full screenshot it produced becomes the new coordinate reference for your next call. IMPORTANT: in this session the individual interaction tools (left_click, type, key, scroll, drag, etc.) are NOT available — this is the ONLY way to click, type, or otherwise interact with the computer. A single action is just a one-item batch.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y) drag start — left_click_drag only. Omit to drag from current cursor.

text.description: For type: the text. For key/hold_key: the chord string. For click/scroll: modifier keys to hold.

State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

The coordinator then clears its activities while other observers still hold a reference to the failed one. Real use waits between turns, so this needs a test to happen. EOF

content.text:
Both parts are done and committed on `claude/no-save-prompts`, not pushed. The nozzle change can no longer drop unsaved edits that exist nowhere else. The "previously opened file" question now appears however the file is opened, and notices when the file has changed.

**Nozzle change (commit d33fb306c9).** You were right that my earlier version could drop edits without keeping them. Only the printer panel's agent saved a version first; the nozzle-change function itself didn't. The function now refuses to switch until the unsaved edits are saved to the project's version history:
- If saving fails, or the caller has no way to save, the nozzle stays as it was and the person is told why.
- The printer panel saves through autosave.
- Tests cover all three cases: no way to save, saving fails, and saving succeeds. In the last, restoring the saved version brings the edits back.

**Reopen question (commit 849b2b516a).** The four screenshots are attached and also in `reopen-prompt-screenshots/` in the worktree. The app drew them itself; I didn't use screen access, since you declined it. On a Mac the default choice is the first, blue button. The generic icon is only because the test app has none.
- **Every way of opening asks:** File > Open Project, recent files, Finder and dragging a file onto the app. Before, only Finder and drag-and-drop asked.
- **Changed files:** each project now remembers which file it came from and a fingerprint of that file's contents. If the file has changed since, the question says so and defaults to "Create new project". Otherwise it defaults to the existing project.
- **The agent:** it no longer opens the file straight away. It gets back the project's name and whether the file changed, along with this instruction: "Ask the person whether to continue that project or start a new one from the file." It then calls again with your answer. This now covers model files (STL and the like) too, which were never matched before.
- **Importing:** adding a file into a project still never asks.

The agent tests (273 cases), the workspace tests (41 cases, plus 5,934 checks in the full-app workspace test) and the AgentUI web tests (410) all pass. So do the end-to-end tests in the default (547 checks), printer (199) and reopen (77) modes.

**One thing to confirm.** Your original brief said not to add any new confirmation step to the agent tools. The reopen question does add one: `project_open` now waits for "existing" or "new" when a file was opened before. I did that on purpose because you asked for the question. Tell me if you'd rather the agent pick a default and just say what it did.

Separately, I found a rare crash risk in existing code. If the agent sends a tool call that fails immediately, right after a new project is created and before that project has been saved even once, the app reads a record that was just deleted. Normal use waits between steps, so I haven't seen it outside my test, and I didn't fix it. It's written up in the untracked report, [no-save-prompts-report.md](no-save-prompts-report.md).

> The agent: it no longer opens the file straight away.
