First, I am pretty sure a old version of the dialogue already existed. Be sure you reuse the old one rather than the duplicating a similar function. Second, the screenshot you show were really ugly. I think other agents have made a similar mistake when they were using system native dialogues rather than the shared dialog the upstream orcaslicer already had. Check to see if you have made the same mistake, if so, fix it in a similar way and add to This as a lesson to the Knowledge Sharing Engineering doc under agent-docs

<!-- reply -->
> Nozzle change (commit d33fb306c9). You were right that my earlier version could drop edits without keeping them. Only the printer panel’s agent saved a version first; the nozzle-change function itself didn’t. The function now refuses to switch until the unsaved edits are saved to the project’s version history:
> 
> If saving fails, or the caller has no way to save, the nozzle stays as it was and the person is told why.
> The printer panel saves through autosave.
> Tests cover all three cases: no way to save, saving fails, and saving succeeds. In the last, restoring the saved version brings the edits back.

When this refusal goes back to the agent, will the agent process in the same way as other orca questions?

No, and it shouldn’t be. They’re two different kinds of result.

An OrcaSlicer question is a warning with code orca_question, returned by settings_preview_patch. It means: this change is valid and will apply as sent, but a person making it by hand would see this question. The agent settles it before applying the patch. It can go ahead, go ahead and tell the user, or ask the user first when the answer is theirs. The guidance for this lives in the settings_preview_patch tool description in ToolRegistry.cpp, not in any prompt.

This refusal is a plain tool error, code change_failed, returned by printer_change. Nothing happened: the nozzle wasn’t changed because the unsaved printer edits couldn’t be saved to version history first. There’s no question to settle and no “go ahead” option. The model handles it like any other failed tool call. It reads the message and decides what to say, and the failed tool card already shows the person the sentence.

Two things follow from that:

There’s no specific guidance for this failure. The printer prompt (printerInstructions.ts) gives instructions after a failed connection (lines 156-157) and for settings the tools refuse (line 59). It says nothing about change_failed from printer_change, and it doesn’t mention orca_question at all. So the agent improvises here, and I haven’t measured what it does.
Making it an OrcaSlicer question would be wrong. That would mean the change applies anyway and the agent decides whether to mention it. The whole point of this refusal is that the nozzle must not change while the edits exist nowhere else. A failed save to version history is a fault to report, not a choice for the user. The useful next step is to try again. Failing that, the person can save or discard the printer edits in Printer settings, then change the nozzle.
If you want the agent to say something consistent here, the fix is one line in the printer prompt about change_failed. That would mean editing prompt text, which the original brief said another task owns, so it’s your call.

So this behavior is wrong too. But let's keep it here. Creates a test chip to look into what's the right way to handle it.


one last thing: orca_questions is a bad name. Rename it to something that would reflect its nature better. If you do not understand why this function was created, go back to git log and In session history to find out. Make sure you give it a relevant name for its purpose and scope. Make sure you change both the code and the document so that it's easier for us to discuss this and for you to think things through when we are making changes related to this function again.

# JusPrin engineering and verification method

**Status:** Required planning, implementation, and release-verification method for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is changing the presentation of a mature manufacturing application. The main engineering risk is not whether common UI technology can work; it is whether new presentation code bypasses, duplicates, or destabilizes authoritative Orca behavior.

## Risk vocabulary

Risk means residual, evidence-backed uncertainty that could materially affect architecture, correctness, delivery, regressions, or a physical print after mature precedent has been considered.

Keep these categories separate:

- **Feasibility:** whether a technical boundary can work at all.
- **Integration:** whether proven components can be connected without unsafe ownership or duplicated behavior.
- **Product behavior:** uncertainty about what the feature must do.
- **Delivery effort:** understood implementation work, even when substantial.
- **Regression exposure:** risk of disturbing mature Orca behavior.
- **Platform QA:** evidence required for a particular OS, WebView backend, display stack, input method, or DPI.

A known bug, untested platform, or inconvenient implementation detail is not automatically an architecture risk.

## Required assessment process

Before adding a spike or assigning a risk label:

1. Define the user-visible requirement without assuming an implementation or cause.

# JusPrin engineering and verification method

**Status:** Required planning, implementation, and release-verification method for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is changing the presentation of a mature manufacturing application. The main engineering risk is not whether common UI technology can work; it is whether new presentation code bypasses, duplicates, or destabilizes authoritative Orca behavior.

## Risk vocabulary

Risk means residual, evidence-backed uncertainty that could materially affect architecture, correctness, delivery, regressions, or a physical print after mature precedent has been considered.

Keep these categories separate:

- **Feasibility:** whether a technical boundary can work at all.
- **Integration:** whether proven components can be connected without unsafe ownership or duplicated behavior.
- **Product behavior:** uncertainty about what the feature must do.
- **Delivery effort:** understood implementation work, even when substantial.
- **Regression exposure:** risk of disturbing mature Orca behavior.
- **Platform QA:** evidence required for a particular OS, WebView backend, display stack, input method, or DPI.

A known bug, untested platform, or inconvenient implementation detail is not automatically an architecture risk.

0f46943de2 Hand OrcaSlicer's edit-time questions to the agent as preview warnings
Hand OrcaSlicer's edit-time questions to the agent as preview warnings

When a person changes certain settings in OrcaSlicer's settings panel,
OrcaSlicer asks a question first: "smooth timelapse needs a prime tower,
enable it?", "this will change the shape of your model, are you sure?",
"change the recommended support settings for you?". The code that asks is
Tab::on_value_change, which runs for one field at a time. The settings tools
apply a patch through Tab::load_config, which never runs it. Since the tools
were allowed to change every setting except a short blacklist (5dadfe2801),
a patch could change these settings and nobody was asked or told.

settings_preview_patch now returns one warning per question, with code
orca_question:

- key: the setting the question is about;
- message: the question as a person would read it, whole;
- suggestions: the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as key=value,
  leaving out any that already hold;
- min and max, for layer height: the nozzles' limits.

The patch stays valid and applies as sent. The agent settles the question
one of three ways, which the tool description spells out: go ahead; go
ahead and tell the user; or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs
to give. Kenneth chose this on 2026-10-12 over refusing the change, holding
it for approval, or blacklisting the settings. A valid tool call already
starts at once, and a "the person agreed" field would only be the agent's
word.

The rules are forward_edit_questions in the new OrcaEditQuestions.hpp, a
copy of the conditions in Tab.cpp for the process, object, filament and
printer scopes: the prime tower with smooth timelapse, clumping detection
or precise Z height; print by object on a bed-slinger; the support
filaments; make_overhang_printable; sparse_infill_rotate_template; layer
height outside the nozzles' limits; the two long retraction switches. No
OrcaSlicer file changes. A question is raised only for a setting the patch
really changes, with its condition read from the values the patch leaves,
so a patch that sends the companion value with the change raises nothing,
and neither does a state a person chose earlier.

give every queued callback an explicit lifetime token; closing a window does not
make captured objects safe.

### A parented top-level shell did not have an independent lifetime

**Observed problem:** The first opaque shell was a top-level `wxFrame` parented
to the legacy OrcaSlicer frame. On macOS, destroying the probe also caused the
tracked legacy frame and shell to be destroyed. A parent relationship chosen for
window stacking had unintentionally coupled the windows' lifetimes.

**Resolution:** The shell became an unparented top-level window. It explicitly
observes legacy move, size, visibility, activation, and destruction events, while
the probe remains owned by the shell. The final run destroyed the probe while
the application, legacy frame, and opaque shell remained alive.

**Lesson for future agents:** Treat wx top-level parenting as lifecycle
ownership, not as a harmless z-order hint. Windows that must survive
independently should have independent ownership and explicit lifecycle
observation.

### Native choice dismissal moved focus to the opaque shell

**Observed problem:** Dismissing the native macOS `wxChoice` popup could leave
the opaque shell as the key window. The probe still existed, but it was no longer
the usable window above the shell.

**Resolution:** The choice handler schedules probe `Raise()` and control
`SetFocus()` calls with `CallAfter`, after the native popup has completed its own
focus transition.

**Lesson for future agents:** Focus after a native popup is asynchronous. Check

new dialog sites, extend the guards and this table, and run the sweep.

### Questions OrcaSlicer asks a person who edits a field

`Tab::on_value_change` in `Tab.cpp` runs when a person changes one field. For
some settings it shows a question first. `Tab::load_config` never runs it, so
a patch changes those settings and nobody is asked. The question goes to the
caller instead.

Kenneth decided this on 2026-10-12. The caller is an agent, and it settles
the question itself, one of three ways: go ahead; go ahead and tell the user;
or ask the user first, when the answer is theirs to give (it depends on what
the object is for, or it accepts a risk to their printer). No tool refuses
these changes, holds them for approval, or records that a person agreed. The
description of `settings_preview_patch` tells the caller this.

Preview adds one warning per question, with code `orca_question`:

- `key` is the setting the question is about.
- `message` is the question as the person would read it, whole. It comes
  from the translation catalog, so it is in the interface language.
- `suggestions` are the values OrcaSlicer's Yes would set, as `key=value`,
  leaving out any that already hold. A caller accepts by adding them to the
  patch.
- `min` and `max`, for layer height, are the nozzles' limits; for a
  first-layer temperature, the values OrcaSlicer saves without asking.

`Tab::save_preset` also asks, per `Tab::validate_filament_temperature_pairs`;
with `persistAs`, preview forwards that as above (`forward_save_questions`).

The warning leaves the patch valid, and the patch applies as sent. The apply
result does not repeat it.

The rules are `forward_edit_questions` in `OrcaEditQuestions.hpp`. They are a
copy of the conditions in `Tab.cpp`, and they look each message up in the
catalog piece by piece, as `Tab.cpp` does. Three things follow from how
OrcaSlicer asks:

- A question is about a setting the patch really changes. A value the
  normalizer puts straight back (clumping detection on a printer without it)
  raises nothing.
- The condition is read from the values the patch leaves. A patch that sends
  the companion value with the change (smooth timelapse together with the
  prime tower) raises nothing.
- A state a person chose earlier by answering "do it anyway" raises nothing
  on a later patch that leaves those settings alone.

An object override raises the same questions as the process setting, because
OrcaSlicer's object panel runs the same handler.

| Setting | OrcaSlicer asks when the change leaves | Yes sets |
|---|---|---|
| `enable_prime_tower` off | smooth `timelapse_type`; and then a second question if `enable_wrapping_detection` is on. Clumping detection alone raises nothing | nothing (No turns the tower back on) |
| `enable_prime_tower` on | `precise_z_height` on | nothing |
| `enable_wrapping_detection` on | the prime tower off | nothing |
| `precise_z_height` on | the prime tower on | nothing |
| `timelapse_type` smooth | the prime tower off | `enable_prime_tower=1` |
| `print_sequence` by object | a printer whose `printer_structure` is `i3` | nothing |
| `support_filament` | a filament OrcaSlicer counts as support material (`is_support_filament`, not strict) that is not soluble, in a project where no object uses TPU | nothing (No sets it back to 0) |
| `support_interface_filament` | a support material without all of top Z distance 0, interface spacing 0 and the interlaced rectilinear pattern; or a soluble interface over a base that is not | those three values, `independent_support_layer_height=0`, and sometimes `support_filament` |
| `make_overhang_printable` on | always | nothing |
| `sparse_infill_rotate_template` given where there was none | a pattern other than rectilinear, line, zigzag, cross zag or locked zag | nothing |
| `layer_height` | a height below the lowest `min_layer_height` or above the highest `max_layer_height` of the printer's nozzles | the nearer limit |
| `long_retractions_when_cut` (printer) or `filament_long_retractions_when_cut` (filament) on for an extruder | always. This one has only an OK button: OrcaSlicer informs, it does not ask | nothing |

The copy is held to the original by the workspace adapter harness. It makes
each change the way a field does (the value into the tab's config, then
OrcaSlicer's own `on_value_change`), with every dialog the handler opens
answered and written down, and compares those dialogs with the questions
preview forwarded. `verify_edit_questions` does this for a case per row and
for the cases that must raise nothing. `verify_every_writable_setting` does
it for every setting it applies, so a question upstream adds, drops or
rewords fails the sweep with `Orca asks ..., preview forwarded ...` and the
setting's name. After an upstream update, run the harness and bring the
rules and this table back in line with `Tab.cpp`.

input.title: Decide how the agent handles a refused nozzle change
input.tldr: Today a nozzle change refuses when the printer's unsaved edits can't be saved to version history, and the agent gets a bare tool error with no guidance. Kenneth says that behavior is wrong too. This task works out the right handling and proposes it.
input.prompt:
Repository: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin (OrcaSlicer fork "JusPrin"). Work in your own git worktree, based on the branch `claude/no-save-prompts` (local, unpushed, in worktree .claude/worktrees/hungry-bartik-ceb424; commits d33fb306c9 and 7852470aff are the relevant ones) or on origin/jusprin-newui once that branch is merged. Do not touch the main checkout or another session's worktree.

Background. On 2026-09-29 Kenneth decided JusPrin never asks a person to save or discard: autosave keeps the work and version history is the way back. On 2026-10-14 the printer nozzle change was changed to follow that rule: `change_named_printer_nozzle` in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp drops the project printer's unsaved edits only after a caller-supplied step (`keep_unsaved_edits`, which pins an autosave version; supplied by ShellController through PrinterPanel::Callbacks) has saved them to version history. If that step is missing or fails, the nozzle is not changed and the function returns the message "The unsaved changes to this printer couldn't be saved to the project's history, so the nozzle was not changed." The printer panel's `printer_change` tool (PrinterConversation::change in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp) turns that into a plain tool error with code `change_failed`.

The open question. Kenneth said this behavior is wrong too, without saying what is right. Today the agent improvises: the printer prompt (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts) has guidance after a failed connection and for refused settings, but nothing about `change_failed` from `printer_change`. It is NOT an OrcaSlicer confirmation (warning code `skipped_confirmation`, returned by settings_preview_patch for a valid patch that applies as sent), and must not become one: the nozzle must never change while the edits exist nowhere else.

What to do: investigate and propose the right handling, for example whether the failure should be retried automatically, carry a distinct error code and recovery steps in the result, change how the panel presents it, or get one sentence of prompt guidance (prompt text is restructured by another task, so coordinate before editing printerInstructions.ts). Read agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md (printer panel section) and agent-docs/jusprin/autosave-version-history.md first. Reproduce the failure path with the shell harness (`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-setup`; checks named nozzle_change_whose_keeper_fails_leaves_unsaved_edits and nozzle_panel_*). Do not call any live model without Kenneth approving a specific batch. Write your proposal for Kenneth in plain English: what happens today, the options with consequences, your recommendation. Do not push.

All four items are done and committed on `claude/no-save-prompts` (not pushed), and every test suite passes. One of my commits doesn't build on its own; fixing that needs your OK, covered at the end.

**1. Reusing the old dialog.** I didn't duplicate it. "Previously opened file" was always the existing handler in `ShellController`, and I extended that handler rather than copying it. The agent's path shows no dialog at all; it reuses the same lookup of earlier projects.

**2. The ugly dialog (commit d7c62b4534).** Yes, I made the same mistake. The old dialog, and my change to it, used `wxMessageDialog`, which on a Mac is a system alert. The earlier fix by another agent is `offer_agent_setup` in `ShellController`, which switched to OrcaSlicer's own `MessageDialog`. I did the same:
- **Button order:** OrcaSlicer's dialog always highlights its Yes button, so I put the suggested choice there. That's "Create new project" when the file changed, and the existing project otherwise.
- **Getting the dialog to the person:** while a person opens a file, the app automatically answers every OrcaSlicer dialog. Switching dialogs alone would have meant this question was cancelled before anyone saw it. A dialog listener can now let one specific dialog through to the person, and this question uses that for itself only.
- **Screenshots:** the new ones are attached.
- **The lesson:** no document is named "Knowledge Sharing Engineering". The one that collects lessons for future agents is `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`, so I added it there. Tell me if you meant a different document.
- **Elsewhere:** other JusPrin code still uses system alerts, mostly error messages in the left pane and status row. I left those alone.

**3. The nozzle-change refusal.** It's unchanged, and a task chip is filed: "Decide how the agent handles a refused nozzle change." The chip states the constraint: the nozzle must never change while the unsaved edits exist nowhere else, so this must not become a skipped confirmation.

**4. The rename (commit dfd89a1379).** `orca_question` is now `skipped_confirmation`. I based the name on the commit that created it: the warning marks a confirmation OrcaSlicer would ask of a person making that change, or saving it, by hand. The patch skips that confirmation and applies as sent, and the agent settles it. It's not a refusal. The rename covers the code, the rule file (now `SkippedConfirmations.hpp`), the test names, the tool description and the tool guide. The guide section is now titled "Skipped confirmations" and notes the old name.

**Tests:** I ran everything again after these changes, and it all passes:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent unit tests | 273 test cases |
| Workspace tests | 41 test cases |
| Full-app workspace test | 5,934 checks |
| End-to-end, default mode | 547 checks |
| End-to-end, printer mode | 199 checks |
| End-to-end, reopen mode | 77 checks |
| Dialog capture | passes |

**One thing needs your OK.** The renamed file was already staged when I made the dialog commit, so the rename landed in d7c62b4534 instead of dfd89a1379. As a result d7c62b4534 doesn't build on its own; the branch tip does. Fixing it means rewriting those two unpushed commits so the rename moves into the second one. Should I do that?

  hook saves it first; a failed save is the tool error. unsavedWork and the

  resets Orca's own save tracker. Its prompt-table row is gone.

  check is now one of them instead of a refusal.

  the person while a file open answers the rest. Recorded as a lesson in

Harness checks cover each path; --reopen-prompt draws the dialog to PNGs.

All my changes are now a single commit, 336facf825, pushed to jusprin-newui as a fast-forward on top of the force-pushed branch. It changes 41 files, adding 836 lines and removing 368, and every test suite passes on that exact commit.

**Rebasing onto the new base:** the force-pushed branch added two commits, one sweeping approval wording out of prompts and docs and one moving the assistant's prompt into the Agent page. My commit conflicted with the wording sweep in three places, all in sentences my commit deletes (the old "discard" instructions for `project_open` and `printer_setup`). The sweep had changed nothing else there, so I kept my side. The moved prompt mentions none of the removed parameters.

**An intermittent failure I fixed before landing:** the first test run on the rebased build failed two reopen checks once.
- **Cause:** autosave could start tracking a freshly opened .3mf before OrcaSlicer had set the project's file name. The project then never recorded which file it came from, so a reopen couldn't tell whether the file had changed.
- **Fix:** when a project's first version is saved, autosave now records the project file if nothing is recorded yet.
- **Evidence:** before the fix, the missing record showed up in about one run in ten. After it, six runs in a row passed.

| End-to-end, default mode | 550 checks pass |

| End-to-end, reopen mode | 77 checks pass |
| Dialog capture | passes |

- The local branch `backup/no-save-prompts-before-squash` holds the six commits before the squash. I can delete it if you don't need it.
